units: Yeb. I, 2 כשם שבתו פטורה כך צָרָתָהּ פטורה as a man’s daughter (who was the wife of his brother that died without issue) is exempt from marrying the yabam (her father), so is her associate exempt.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 1:2">Ib.</cite> <he>הלכה צָרַת בתו … כשם שצָרַת בתו פטורה כך צרת צרתה פטורה</he> if this his daughter’s associate marries a second brother of his who has another wife besides her, and he dies (without issue): as his daughter’s former associate is exempt, so is the latter’s present associate exempt; a. v. fr.—

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 103b:15">Snh. 103ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Yoma 9b:5">Yoma 9ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 7:10">Num. R. s. 7</cite> <he>מסכה צ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="M01943"><he>מַסֵּכָה</he> I</cite>.

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 101:2">Midr. Till. to Ps. CI</cite> <he>ועבר בים צ׳ זה צלמו של מיכה</he> ‘and a rival crossed the sea’ (<cite ref="Zechariah 10:11">Zech. X, 11</cite>) , that means the image of Micah; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 16:26">Num. R. s. 16</cite>, end; Mekh. Bo, s. 14.—

Yeb. I, 1 צרותיהן, חמש … פוטרות נָרוֹתֵיהֶן צ׳ fifteen women (married severally to the brother of a man with whom marriage is forbidden) cause the exemption from yibbum (יִבּוּם) of their associates and eventually the associates of their associates.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 1:4">Ib. 4</cite> <he>בית שמאי מתירין הצ׳ לאחים</he> the school of Shammai allows the rivals of a woman forbidden on account of consanguinity to be married to one of the brothers of the deceased (without issue); a. fr.
